description: A double pendulum worked out sample by sample, for smooth chaotic control voltages

params.text: Sets the length of the two rods, a micrometre at the far left to a metre at the far right, a millimetre at the centre; short rods swing fast and long ones slowly
Sets the gravity the pendulum falls under, marked with the surface gravity of Pluto, the Moon, Mercury, Earth, Jupiter and the Sun
Sets how much friction slows the swinging, none at the far left; this one takes effect straight away rather than waiting for a start
Sets both rods to an angle of π and starts them swinging, taking the length and gravity settings as they stand at that moment

inputs.text: Sets the length of the rods along with its knob, but only when the pendulum is started
Sets the gravity along with its knob, but only when the pendulum is started
Adds to the friction knob, a volt covering a tenth of its travel, and it takes effect straight away
A reading above 2.5V sets both rods to an angle of π and starts them swinging

outputs.text: The horizontal position of the first mass, -5V to +5V
The height of the first mass, 0V to 10V
The horizontal position of the second mass, -5V to +5V
The height of the second mass, 0V to 10V
5V for as long as the first rod's angle is zero, dropping back to 0V once that angle reaches π or stops changing
5V for as long as the second rod's angle is zero, dropping back to 0V once that angle reaches π or stops changing

notes: the length and gravity settings are only read at a start, so turning those knobs does nothing until the button is pressed or a gate arrives
the number of polyphony channels is the widest of the four inputs, and each channel runs its own pendulum
menu: x₂ y₂ relative — measures the second mass from the first rather than from the fixed pivot

inputs.3:
high above 2.5V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
